There were coexistence pacts in 1854 and 1855, but the two governments competed for trade and for influence over the provinces until the war of 1859.

hechos/presidencia-de-urquiza/resumen.texto: Urquiza took office on March 5, 1854 as the first constitutional president of the Confederation, with a provisional capital in Paraná and without Buenos Aires or its customs. His government organized the Congress, promoted immigration and agricultural colonization, nationalized the University of Córdoba, and sought to attract direct trade with customs laws, but it lived with a permanent deficit. He ended his term in 1860, after defeating Buenos Aires at Cepeda.

hechos/parana-capital-de-la-confederacio.texto: Because Buenos Aires was not part of the Confederation, the national government settled in Paraná in 1854, and an Urquiza decree of March 24, 1854 federalized the entire territory of Entre Ríos, which came under the national government. The presidency and the Congress operated there until the dissolution of the Confederation’s government in December 1861.

hechos/derechos-diferenciales-1856-1859/.texto: So that ships could arrive directly at Rosario and the Confederation’s other ports without unloading first in Buenos Aires, the Congress of Paraná doubled in 1856 the import duties on goods that had passed through another Río de la Plata port. Rosario grew, but merchants kept depending on credit and on Buenos Aires ships. The porteño government took it as an aggression, and the tension was one of the causes of the war of 1859.

hechos/asesinato-de-benavidez/resumen.texto: On October 23, 1858, former federal governor Nazario Benavídez, imprisoned by order of the liberal government of San Juan, was murdered in his cell. The Confederation’s government intervened in the province, and the event deepened the rupture between the Confederation and Buenos Aires, whose press supported the liberals of San Juan.

hechos/batalla-de-cepeda-1859/resumen.texto: On October 23, 1859, the Confederation army under Urquiza defeated the Buenos Aires army, commanded by Bartolomé Mitre, in the cañada of Cepeda, near the boundary between Buenos Aires and Santa Fe. Mitre withdrew to Buenos Aires, and Urquiza advanced to San José de Flores, where peace was negotiated.

hechos/firma-del-pacto-de-san-jose-de-fl.texto: Pact of San José de Flores

On November 11, 1859, with the mediation of Francisco Solano López, Buenos Aires agreed to join the Confederation. It could propose reforms to the Constitution and would keep its property, except for the customs, which would pass to the nation in exchange for guaranteeing the porteño budget for five years. Valentín Alsina had resigned the governorship before the signing.

hechos/convencion-reformadora-de-1860/re.texto: A Buenos Aires convention proposed reforms to the Constitution of 1853 in 1860, and the National Convention meeting in Santa Fe approved them in September 1860. With them, Buenos Aires swore the Constitution, it was secured that the capital would be fixed by law with the agreement of the ceding province, and the national government’s intervention in the provinces was limited.

hechos/presidencia-de-derqui/resumen.texto: Santiago Derqui took office on March 5, 1860 and attempted an alliance with Mitre, governor of Buenos Aires. It broke down over the San Juan crisis and over Congress’s rejection of the porteño deputies elected under the Buenos Aires law. After Pavón, and without Urquiza’s support, he resigned on November 5, 1861 and went to Montevideo.

hechos/rinconada-del-pocito/titulo.texto: Battle of Rinconada del Pocito and Death of Aberastain

hechos/rinconada-del-pocito/resumen.texto: After the assassination of the federal governor of San Juan, José Antonio Virasoro (November 16, 1860), the national government sent Juan Saá as intervenor. On January 11, 1861, Saá defeated the liberal governor Antonino Aberastain at Rinconada del Pocito, and Aberastain was executed by firing squad the next day. Buenos Aires denounced the execution, and the crisis led to war.

hechos/batalla-de-pavon/resumen.texto: On September 17, 1861, the Buenos Aires army, under Mitre, faced the Confederation army, commanded by Urquiza, beside the Pavón stream. The Confederation’s cavalry defeated the porteño cavalry, but Mitre’s infantry held, and Urquiza withdrew to Entre Ríos with his reserve divisions almost intact, leaving the field and the war to Mitre. The documents do not clarify why he withdrew: his health, his distrust of Derqui, and an understanding with Mitre or with Freemasonry have all been cited. Revisionist authors presented it as a betrayal, and liberal historiography as the victory that made national unity possible.

hechos/matanza-de-canada-de-gomez/resume.texto: On November 22, 1861, porteño troops under the Uruguayan Venancio Flores surprised the Confederation forces’ camp at Cañada de Gómez at dawn and killed a large number of soldiers, many of them already surrendered. The death toll differs by source, and some authors call it a battle and others a massacre.

hechos/presidencia-de-juan-esteban-peder.texto: Presidency of Pedernera and Dissolution of the Confederation

When Derqui resigned, Vice President Juan Esteban Pedernera was left in charge of the national government. Without an army or resources, and with the provinces going over to Mitre, on December 12, 1861 he declared the national executive power in recess. The provinces delegated to Mitre the provisional government of the country, and in 1862 he was elected president.

hechos/presidencia-de-carlos-antonio-lop.texto: Government of Carlos Antonio López in Paraguay

Carlos Antonio López governed Paraguay as consul from 1841 and as president from 1844 until his death in 1862. He formally proclaimed independence in 1842, opened the country to trade after Rosas’s fall, and undertook works with foreign technicians, such as a railway and an iron foundry. He left power to his son Francisco Solano López.

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-britanico/.texto: Founding of the British Hospital of Buenos Aires
A group of British residents led by the Reverend Barton Lodge founded a hospital in 1844 to care for the poor members of their community. It is one of the country’s first community hospitals.

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-frances/ti.texto: Founding of the French Hospital of Buenos Aires

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-frances/re.texto: The French Philanthropic Society, created around 1832 by the French consul and French residents, sustained medical care for its community, which became the French Hospital, inaugurated in 1845 according to its institutional history.

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-italiano/t.texto: Founding of the Italian Hospital of Buenos Aires

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-italiano/r.texto: The Italian Benevolent Society founded the Italian Hospital in 1853. It first received sick members of the community and had its first building of its own in 1872. Today it is a university hospital.

hechos/fundacion-del-colegio-del-uruguay.texto: Founding of the Colegio del Uruguay

Urquiza, governor of Entre Ríos, founded in 1849 in Concepción del Uruguay a secondary school, free for many of its students, which received students from throughout the Litoral. Leaders of the next generation came out of it, such as Julio Argentino Roca and Olegario Víctor Andrade.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-universidad-de-la.texto: Inauguration of the University of the Republic
The university of Montevideo, created by law in 1833, was inaugurated on July 18, 1849, during the siege of the city in the Guerra Grande, with Lorenzo Fernández as its first rector.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-colonia-esperanza.texto: Under the contract Aarón Castellanos signed in 1853 with the government of Santa Fe, about two hundred families of Swiss, German, French, and Italian farmers arrived in 1856. They received land, seed, and animals, to be paid for with part of the harvests. It is generally considered the first organized agricultural colony in the country, and it became the model for colonization in Santa Fe.

hechos/primer-ferrocarril-argentino/resu.texto: The Buenos Aires Western Railway, formed by porteño capitalists with support from the government of the State of Buenos Aires, opened its first section, about ten kilometers long, on August 29, 1857, between the Parque station, where the Teatro Colón stands today, and Floresta. The English-built locomotive La Porteña made the first trip.

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-aleman/tit.texto: Founding of the German Hospital of Buenos Aires

hechos/fundacion-del-hospital-aleman/res.texto: The associations of the German-speaking community of Buenos Aires created the German Hospital on August 26, 1867.

hechos/guerras-civiles-argentinas/resume.texto: A series of internal conflicts that began while the War of Independence was still going on, with Artigas's break with Buenos Aires in January 1814; the Liga Federal formed in 1815. Then came the Directorate and the Congress, dissolved after Cepeda (1820), and provinces governed by caudillos. The period runs from 1814 to 1853, up to the Constitution, with infrequent skirmishes until the federalization of Buenos Aires in 1880. Federalists and Unitarians, or Buenos Aires and the provinces, disagreed over the form of government and over control of the port and customs revenues.

lugares/parana/resumen.texto: City in Entre Ríos, on the Paraná River, born as the Bajada del Paraná in the 18th century. It was the capital of the Argentine Confederation between 1854 and 1861, while Buenos Aires was separate, and it is the capital of Entre Ríos province.

lugares/rosario/resumen.texto: City and port on the Paraná, in southern Santa Fe, declared a city in 1852. With the free navigation of the rivers and the differential duties, it became the Confederation’s main port, and later the country’s great grain port.

lugares/esperanza-santa-fe/resumen.texto: City in central Santa Fe that was born in 1856 as an agricultural colony for European families brought by Aarón Castellanos’s contract. It is generally considered the first organized agricultural colony in the country.

lugares/colegio-del-uruguay/resumen.texto: Secondary school founded by Urquiza in 1849 in Concepción del Uruguay, one of the oldest in the country. It trained much of the Litoral’s leadership in the second half of the 19th century.

lugares/palacio-san-jose/resumen.texto: Urquiza’s residence, built from 1848 near Concepción del Uruguay, from where he governed Entre Ríos and received the leaders of the Confederation. He was assassinated there on April 11, 1870. Today it is a museum.

lugares/casa-del-acuerdo/resumen.texto: House in San Nicolás de los Arroyos where the governors signed the Agreement of San Nicolás on May 31, 1852. Today it is a museum.

lugares/barranca-yaco/resumen.texto: Stretch of the royal road in northern Córdoba province where Facundo Quiroga and his retinue were murdered on February 16, 1835. A monument commemorates the event.

lugares/playa-de-la-agraciada/resumen.texto: Beach in the Uruguayan department of Soriano, on the Uruguay River, where the Thirty-Three Orientals landed on April 19, 1825.

lugares/bahia-blanca/resumen.texto: City and port in southern Buenos Aires province, founded in 1828 as the Fortaleza Protectora Argentina. For decades it was a frontier post facing Indigenous peoples, and later a major grain export port.

lugares/universidad-de-la-republica/resu.texto: Public university of Uruguay, based in Montevideo, created by law in 1833 and inaugurated in 1849. For more than a century it was the country’s only university.

lugares/hospital-britanico-de-buenos-air.texto: Hospital founded in 1844 by the British community of Buenos Aires to care for its poor members. Today it is a private community hospital.

lugares/hospital-frances-de-buenos-aires.texto: Hospital of the French community of Buenos Aires, arising from the French Philanthropic Society and inaugurated in 1845 according to its institutional history. Today it belongs to PAMI.

lugares/hospital-italiano-de-buenos-aire.texto: Hospital founded in 1853 by the Italian Benevolent Society of Buenos Aires for the Italian community. Today it is a high-complexity university hospital.

lugares/hospital-aleman-de-buenos-aires/.texto: Hospital created in 1867 by the associations of the German-speaking community of Buenos Aires.
